_about: Lucky Monkey rules. Edit, then `tools/deploy.sh data` (seconds, no rebuild). Missing keys fall back to the built-in copy. See docs/ for what each part means.

workers.name: Mango
workers.role: Field technician: walks the links, fixes anything, swings on vines for 🍌.

workers.name: Pip
workers.role: Scout: flies straight over the void and diagnoses fast; too small for heavy work.

workers.name: Moss
workers.role: Maintenance: slow to travel, twice as fast at preventive work (certificates, patches, clean-ups, canaries).

tutorial.coach: A service crashed. Press Space (or click the 💻 terminal), then pick 🔄 Restart. A worker walks there and fixes it.
Names don't resolve but IPs work: that's DNS. Not sure? 🔍 Diagnose (I) shows which option fixes the cause.
A WARNING: nothing is broken yet. The big TIME TO LOSS timer counts down. Renew the certificate before it hits; Moss 🦥 is fastest at maintenance.
Two at once! Pick a worker in the roster (Z/X/C) before choosing a fix, so each one takes a different job.

crash.name: Service crashed
crash.symptom: The service process exited. The machine still answers ping, but its port is closed.

restart.note: The process is back; the logs show a one-off crash.

dns.name: DNS resolution failing
dns.symptom: Clients can't resolve hostnames. Connecting by IP address still works, but nobody remembers the numbers.

fixdns.note: Resolver configuration restored; names resolve again.

restart.note: The restart reloaded the cache, but the bad config returns as records expire.

dhcp.name: DHCP pool exhausted
dhcp.symptom: No addresses left in the pool. New devices get no lease and fall back to 169.254.x.x, which can't reach anything.

expandpool.note: The pool is widened from /26 to /24; new devices get leases.

restart.note: Restarting doesn't create addresses: the pool is still full.

cable.name: Damaged cable
cable.symptom: 20% packet loss and CRC errors on one port. A crocodile chewed the patch cable.

replacecable.note: New cable fitted; the CRC errors are gone. It was the physical layer.

restart.note: Software restarts don't fix a damaged cable (layer 1).

route.name: Missing route
route.symptom: The router lost its route to the southern islands; packets come back as ICMP 'destination unreachable'.

fixroute.note: The static route is restored; traffic flows again.

failover.note: The standby router works for now, but its routing table is stale.

ddos.name: DDoS flood
ddos.symptom: Requests ×40 from thousands of sources. A stampede is hammering one endpoint.

blockacl.note: Firewall ACL drops the attacking sources; real users get through.

ratelimit.note: Rate limiting buys time but also turns away some real users. The attack continues.

restart.note: Restarting doesn't stop traffic that is still arriving.

worm.name: Worm infection
worm.symptom: An unknown process copies itself over every connection it can reach.

warning.text: A worm signature is circulating and this node is unpatched.

patch.note: Patched and cleaned; the hole it used is closed.

quarantine.note: Isolated on its own VLAN: it can't spread, but it's still infected.

restart.note: The worm survives reboots: it's in the startup scripts.

cert.name: Expired TLS certificate
cert.symptom: Clients reject the TLS handshake: the certificate's validity date has passed.

warning.text: The TLS certificate expires soon. Renew it now and nobody notices.

disabletls.note: Refused: turning off TLS would send passwords in clear text. Renew the certificate instead.

leak.name: Memory leak
leak.symptom: RAM use grows 2 GB a minute and the system is swapping. Something never frees its memory.

patch.note: The code that never freed memory is fixed.

restart.note: Memory is freed for now; the leak will fill RAM again.

failover.note: The standby takes over with clean memory; the same bug leaks there too.

disk.name: Disk full
disk.symptom: Disk at 100%. Writes fail and logs can't rotate.

warning.text: Disk at 85% and climbing: old snapshots are piling up.

cleanup.note: Old snapshots removed; writes work again.

heat.name: Thermal throttling
heat.symptom: CPU at 98 °C and throttling its clock speed: the vents are clogged with leaves.

clearvents.note: Vents cleared; the temperature is back to 55 °C.

restart.note: It cooled while rebooting; it will heat up again.

power.name: Power supply failed
power.symptom: Lightning hit the rack and the primary power supply is dead. The redundant one is idle.

failover.note: Switched to the redundant power supply.

restart.note: Nothing to restart: there's no power.

deploy.name: Bad deploy
deploy.symptom: v2.4 went out and the error rate is 30%. There was no schema change: v2.3 is still compatible.

warning.text: A deploy of v2.4 is scheduled. Canary it first: a bad build then reaches only a few users.

rollback.note: Back on v2.3, which is compatible: the errors stop.

fallforward.note: No hotfix is ready yet. v2.3 is compatible, so rolling back is faster and safe.

restart.note: Restarting runs the same broken v2.4.

migration.name: Bad deploy with migration
migration.symptom: v2.4 migrated the database schema and the error rate is 30%. v2.3 can't read the new tables.

fallforward.note: Hotfix v2.4.1 shipped; it works with the new schema.

rollback.note: v2.3 can't read the migrated schema: rolling back would break it further.

disparity.name: Replica disparity
disparity.symptom: The replicas' checksums disagree: two copies report two different banana counts.

resync.note: Replicas re-copied from the primary; the checksums match.

loop.name: Routing loop
loop.symptom: Packets circle between two routers until their IP TTL (a hop count) reaches 0 and they're dropped.

fixroute.note: The route that pointed back is fixed; packets reach their destination.

restart.note: Routes were relearned, but the bad static route returns.

broadcast.name: Broadcast storm
broadcast.symptom: A looped cable floods the switch with broadcasts; Spanning Tree was turned off on this switch.

enablestp.note: STP blocked the redundant port; the storm stops.

replacecable.note: The cables are fine; it's the loop they form.

vlan.name: VLAN misconfiguration
vlan.symptom: Ports were put on the wrong VLAN: the tree frogs can't reach their default gateway.

fixvlan.note: Ports are back on VLAN 20; the gateway answers.

restart.note: The port configuration survives a restart.

fixvlan.label: Move ports to the right VLAN

timeloss.name: Time to Loss (game term)
timeloss.text: Lucky Monkey's own timer: seconds until the next consequence. Not IP TTL (a hop count) and not DNS TTL (how long a record may be cached).

process.name: Processes and ports
process.text: A service is a running process listening on a port. The machine can be up (it answers ping) while the service is dead.

dns.name: DNS
dns.text: The Domain Name System turns names into IP addresses. If it fails, connections by IP still work, but names don't.

dhcp.name: DHCP
dhcp.text: DHCP hands out IP addresses from a pool, as time-limited leases. With an empty pool, new devices get no address.

physical.name: Physical layer
physical.text: Layer 1: cables, ports and signals. CRC errors and packet loss on one port often mean a bad cable, which no software fixes.

routing.name: Routing
routing.text: Routers forward packets using a routing table. Without a route, the packet is dropped and ICMP reports 'destination unreachable'.

ddos.name: DDoS
ddos.text: A distributed denial of service floods a target from many sources. Rate limits buy time; filtering the sources (ACLs) stops it.

patching.name: Patching and segmentation
patching.text: Worms exploit unpatched holes and spread across the network. Isolating a node (a separate VLAN) stops the spread; patching removes the hole.

tls.name: TLS certificates
tls.text: TLS encrypts connections and proves identity with a certificate that expires. Renew it before it does; never just turn encryption off.

memory.name: Memory and swap
memory.text: A leak keeps claiming RAM until the system swaps to disk and crawls. A restart frees it for a while; only a code fix stops it.

storage.name: Storage capacity
storage.text: A full disk makes every write fail. Rebooting doesn't free space: delete or move data, or add capacity.

thermal.name: Thermal throttling
thermal.text: Hot CPUs slow themselves down to survive. Cooling (airflow, clean vents) is the fix.

redundancy.name: Redundancy and failover
redundancy.text: A spare component (a second power supply, a standby server) takes over when the primary fails, if one was there to begin with.

rollback.name: Rollback
rollback.text: Undo a bad change by going back to the previous version, as long as that version still works with today's data.

migration.name: Schema migrations
migration.text: A deploy that changes the database schema can't simply be rolled back: the old version can't read the new tables. Fix forward.

replication.name: Replication
replication.text: Replicas are copies of a database. When they disagree, re-copy them from the authoritative primary.

ipttl.name: IP TTL
ipttl.text: Each IP packet carries a TTL hop count; every router subtracts 1, and at 0 the packet is dropped. That stops a routing loop from circling forever.

stp.name: Spanning Tree
stp.text: STP finds loops between switches and blocks a redundant port, so broadcasts can't circle and multiply into a storm.

vlan.name: VLANs
vlan.text: VLANs split one switch into separate networks. A port on the wrong VLAN can't reach its own subnet's default gateway.

notices.text: Cache hit ratio 94% at {node}: most requests never touch the database.
{node}: CPU 61 °C, a little warm but within limits.
Unusual traffic to {node}: just the tree frogs' weekly sync.
{node}: cached DNS records expired after their TTL (300 s) and were refreshed.
Bandwidth between the islands at 40%: plenty of headroom.
